Nunuïko Display

The straight-terminal display cut of Nunito Sans, proofed live against its source. Both columns render real four-axis variable fonts — stock Nunito Sans and the current Nunuïko Display build — so what you see is what ships. Use the Roman / Italic switch to proof either script (14 roman + 13 italic masters).

Waterfall — UI sizes

The range that matters for interface text. The l / I / 1 triplet leads each line: the shortened tail must stay a visible disambiguator down to 9 px. Adjust the axes above — the ramp follows.

Glyph focus — the four edits and their composites

Each row: source, current build, then an overlay at the same origin (colour fringing marks the change). All rows follow the axis sliders.

14 · l — plain stem like I by default (Display doesn't disambiguate Il1; Nunuïko does). The tailed l (edit 01) is now ss02. Composites (fl, ffl, lá, ľ, ŀl, ł) follow.

Nunito Sans

l fl lá ľ ŀl ł Il1

Nunuïko Display

l fl lá ľ ŀl ł Il1
l fl lá ľ ŀl ł Il1
l fl lá ľ ŀl ł Il1

Nunuïko Display with ss02: tailed l

l fl lá ľ ŀl ł Il1

02 · f — top terminal rotated 10° into a downturn (re-judged from Nunito's 12° for the straight cut). fi is edited too; fl inherits.

Nunito Sans

f fi fl ff ffi ffl fjord

Nunuïko Display

f fi fl ff ffi ffl fjord
f fi fl ff ffi ffl fjord
f fi fl ff ffi ffl fjord

04 · Q — Jost-style straight slash with round caps, crossing the bottom-right ring; counter stays open at every weight.

Q QU Query IQ
Q QU Query IQ

05 · J — U-hook foot, widened to 0.66× U, ending in a flat cut. IJ / NJ / Ĵ track the widening.
